topic: Pen-tip optical flow: DeltaPen hardware and pipeline
citation: Lüthi G., Fender A.R., Holz C. (2022). DeltaPen: A Device with Integrated High-Precision Translation and Rotation Sensing on Passive Surfaces. UIST '22, ACM, 12 pp.
task_or_setup: Prototype pen: two adjacent lens-less optical flow sensors on a tip PCB (rotated apart to maximise optical-centre separation), 3-axis accelerometer + magnetometer (InvenSense MPU9250 incl. AK8963; gyroscope unused), 8 mm FSR on the tip, wide-band LRA haptics; all fusion on a Teensy 4.0 (ARM Cortex-M7, 600 MHz); yaw from the difference of the two flow vectors.
participants_or_bench: Single prototype; engineering description and authors' operating-range observations
comparator: PixArt PMW3360 lens-based mouse sensor (datasheet comparison in text)
key_quantitative_findings: Sensors: 2x PixArt P3040 (lens-less), each reporting motion at 1000 Hz with NOMINAL resolution 6000 dpi (= 4.23 um/count, derived). P3040 tracks up to 200 mm from the surface but 'increasingly unreliably above a distance of 60 mm'; trackable surface typically detected within 20 mm; clutch by lifting ~2 cm. Tip PCB 10 mm x 12 mm; pen 190 mm long, 15 mm diameter. Both sensors on one 3-wire SPI bus. Accelerometer logged at 200 Hz, magnetometer at 100 Hz; FSR sampled at 200 Hz (13-bit ADC). Raw-flow outliers ~0.05% of samples (rejected by thresholding). Rotation: d_alpha = arcsin( s x (s+o) / (|s|*|s+o|) ), s = vector between optical centres, o = difference of the two sensors' motion vectors; tilt ('DPI') correction dx = x_raw/cos(theta), dy = y_raw/cos(psi) from the gravity vector; tip-offset compensation. End-to-end latency stated only as 'comparable to the latency of a tethered computer mouse' (no number). Sensor baseline |s| NOT reported numerically (bounded by the 10 x 12 mm PCB; diagonal 15.6 mm, derived). No numeric tilt limits reported.
units_and_conditions: Tethered: USB supplies power and data; processing on-pen; host receives processed motion; HID-mouse mode available.
locator: Sec. 3.1 Hardware (p.4) + Fig. 2; Sec. 3.2 Embedded processing + Fig. 3 (p.5); Sec. 3.3 Steps 1-7 (pp.5-6); Sec. 6 Limitations; Acknowledgments (PixArt provided the sensors)
limitations: Latency, sensor baseline and usable tilt range not quantified; no public P3040 datasheet found (sensors supplied by PixArt); tethered; gyroscope unused; absolute initial yaw needs a calibration step (Sec. 6).
relevance_to_design: Closest published precedent for pen-tip, lens-less, 1 kHz relative motion sensing that leaves room for a real ballpoint tip - the local paper-relative measurement the stabiliser needs.
transferability_reason: Same form factor (pen with real tip) and measurand (motion relative to the surface); differences are the actuated nib, paper vs tablet surface and an untethered power budget.
design_implication: Use dual lens-less flow sensors + IMU as the reference architecture for the research pen; request P3040 (or successor) samples and datasheet from PixArt early; keep the actuated nib out of the sensors' field of view; measure latency explicitly because DeltaPen does not report it.
search_query: https://static.siplab.org/papers/uist2022-deltapen.pdf

topic: Pen-tip optical flow: DeltaPen measured accuracy and drift
citation: Lüthi G., Fender A.R., Holz C. (2022). DeltaPen (UIST '22), technical evaluation (Sec. 4).
task_or_setup: DeltaPen rigidly coupled tip-to-tip to a Wacom pen on a Wacom Intuos 4; tasks: small (2-4 cm) and large (~10 cm) shapes for 1 min each, 5 sentences in block and cursive, ~5 min free sketch, shapes while hovering; offline comparison of pipeline variants with a GLMM.
participants_or_bench: 10 participants (4 female), aged 25-31 (mean 26.7); 209,986 data points after cleaning
comparator: Translation: deltas of Wacom Intuos 4 absolute positions; yaw: OptiTrack (3 IR cameras)
key_quantitative_findings: MEASURED translation error (magnitude, per 10 ms window): MAE 0.0683 mm, median 0.0236 mm (MAE ~16 counts of the 6000 dpi nominal resolution, derived). Yaw error per 40 ms window (rad): unprocessed median 5.25e-3 / mean 9.56e-3; with magnetometer damping median 4.75e-3 (0.27 deg) / mean 9.19e-3 (0.53 deg); tilt 'DPI correction' made yaw error worse (median 5.60e-3). Accumulated angular drift 0.160e-2 rad/s (0.092 deg/s) over all samples. Idle drift: yaw 9.07e-5 rad/s; translation 0.04375 mm/s in each of X and Y (= 2.6 mm/min, derived). Relative translation error (MdAPE) decreases with speed; Y error consistently larger than X; top velocity bin >= 11.875 cm/s.
units_and_conditions: Surface = Wacom Intuos 4 (not paper); samples within ~1 cm of the surface with clear OptiTrack view; X/Y errors computed after compensating absolute rotation; desk/table use shown only qualitatively.
locator: Sec. 4.1-4.4; Table 1 (p.7); Fig. 6-7 and paragraphs 'Angular drift', 'Idle Drift', 'Translation errors' (p.8)
limitations: No paper surfaces, no tilt sweep and no latency measurement; per-window errors are not stroke-level position errors; small young sample; Wacom ground truth has its own error; evaluated by the device's developers.
relevance_to_design: Only published measured accuracy/drift for a lens-less pen-tip flow pen; sets expectations for relative-motion quality available to the tremor controller and to stroke capture.
transferability_reason: Measured on a tablet surface with the pen coupled to a Wacom stylus; paper texture, ink trails and nib actuation can change flow quality.
design_implication: Budget ~0.07 mm MAE per 10 ms and ~2.6 mm/min idle translation drift for relative sensing; adequate for short-horizon stabilisation but page-level capture needs absolute re-anchoring; replicate this protocol on paper types with a tilt sweep and a latency measurement.
search_query: https://static.siplab.org/papers/uist2022-deltapen.pdf

topic: Pen-tip optical flow: Flashpen (PMW3360 in a pen tip)
citation: Romat H., Fender A., Meier M., Holz C. (2021). Flashpen: A High-Fidelity and High-Precision Multi-Surface Pen for Virtual Reality. IEEE VR 2021, pp. 306-315.
task_or_setup: Pen with a PixArt PMW3360 gaming-mouse sensor at the tip (lens and cover sanded down; flat tip on a cut LEGO hinge with 110 deg range), MPU6500 IMU and ESP32 tethered to a PC; flow sensor used on-surface, 2 OptiTrack Flex13 cameras give hover position and absolute yaw; tracing and writing blocks vs a Wacom pen.
comparator: Wacom professional drawing tablet pen; ordinary pen on paper (writing block)
key_quantitative_findings: Sensor run at 8,000 fps in burst mode; NOMINAL motion resolution stated as 1/226 mm (4.42 um); authors compare with ~200 Hz tablet digitisers. MEASURED tracing accuracy (mean shortest distance to reference normalised by shape width of 1/2/3 cm): ACCURATE instruction Flashpen 0.028 vs Wacom 0.026; FAST instruction 0.076 vs 0.079; no device x speed interaction (F1,9 = 0.80, p = 0.393). Pen mass ~200 g. Authors: works on 'most surface types (wood, paper, plastic and many more)', not glass.
units_and_conditions: Absolute yaw from cameras throughout (flow alone cannot give page orientation); tethered; Oculus Quest 2 via Link.
locator: Abstract; Sec. 3.1-3.2 (pp.3-4), Fig. 2-3; Sec. 5.1 (Block 1 results); Sec. 7 Limitations
limitations: Flat mouse-like contact tip, not a ballpoint; relies on external cameras for yaw and hover; writing block weaker than tracing; surface list qualitative; heavy prototype.
relevance_to_design: Shows a lens-based gaming sensor reaches tablet-like tracing fidelity at 8 kHz - but only with a flat contact tip at fixed height and an external yaw reference.
transferability_reason: Same sensor class; tip geometry and dependence on external tracking differ from a stand-alone ballpoint stabiliser.
design_implication: Use PMW33xx-class sensors on the bench rig (fixed Z) as the high-rate reference; in a ballpoint pen they need custom optics or a lens-less part; provide yaw from a second flow sensor or IMU/magnetometer rather than assuming it.

topic: Optical navigation sensors: PMW3360 / PMW3389 (lens-based, contact height)
citation: PixArt Imaging Inc. PMW3360DM-T2QU Product Datasheet, Version 1.30 (6 Apr 2016); PixArt Imaging Inc. PMW3389DM-T3QU Product Datasheet, Version 1.01 (3 Jan 2019, doc 11020AENW).
task_or_setup: Gaming-mouse navigation sensors with integrated IR illumination, 16-pin DIP, designed for the LM19-LSI 1:1 lens; 4-wire SPI.
participants_or_bench: Manufacturer characterisation on PixArt standard gaming surfaces (QCK, Vespula, FUNC 1030 etc.)
key_quantitative_findings: PMW3360: frame rate up to 12,000 fps (83 us/frame, derived); NOMINAL resolution up to 12,000 cpi in 100 cpi steps (2.1 um/count, derived); resolution error 1% typ (up to 200 ips on QCK at 5000 cpi); speed 250 ips typ; acceleration 50 g max; lens reference plane to surface Z = 2.2 / 2.4 / 2.6 mm (min/typ/max); lift detection 2 mm or 3 mm, or manual lift-cut-off calibration; SPI clock <= 2 MHz; burst-mode address-to-data delay tSRAD_MOTBR = 35 us (so a 6-byte motion burst takes ~59 us at 2 MHz, derived); SROM download registers (firmware upload at start-up). PMW3389: up to 16,000 cpi (50 cpi steps), 400 ips typ, 50 g, Z 2.2-2.6 mm, lift cut-off 2 or 3 mm, run current 21 mA incl. LED at VDD 1.9 V, package 10.90 x 16.20 x 5.01 mm, self-adjusting frame rate (maximum not in key parameters). Both datasheets plot mean resolution and path error versus Z (about 2.0-2.9 mm), i.e. the count scale depends on height.
units_and_conditions: Z plots: straight 4-inch line at 45 deg, 6 ips, 5000 cpi, on gaming mats; no paper, no tilt data.
locator: PMW3360 v1.30: p.1 Key Parameters; operating-conditions table (Z, speed, ResErr, acceleration); AC timing table (tSRAD_MOTBR); Fig. 12-13 (p.17). PMW3389 v1.01: p.1 Key Parameters; operating-conditions table (Z, lift cut-off); Fig. 11-12
limitations: Gaming-mat characterisation at fixed Z; +/-0.2 mm Z tolerance is incompatible with a tilting pen without redesigned optics; documents obtained from distributor mirrors.
relevance_to_design: Highest-rate, lowest-latency commodity motion sensors; ideal as the bench-rig reference channel over paper at controlled height.
transferability_reason: Electrical and timing data transfer directly; optical geometry (2.4 mm Z, flat contact) does not fit a tilted ballpoint tip.
design_implication: Put a PMW3360/3389 on a fixed-height carriage in the bench rig (8-12 kHz frames, ~0.1 ms read latency); do not base the product on them unless custom optics hold Z within +/-0.2 mm across tilt.

topic: Optical navigation sensors: PAA5100JE (near-field) and PMW3901 (far-field) flow chips
citation: PixArt Imaging Inc. PAA5100JE-Q Optical Tracking Chip Product Datasheet, Version 1.00 (25 Jul 2018); PixArt Imaging Inc. PMW3901MB-TXQT Optical Motion Tracking Chip Product Datasheet, Version 1.00 (20 Mar 2017) and Version 1.10 (20 Jun 2017); Pimoroni PMW3901 breakout listing.
task_or_setup: Optical-flow chips with fixed lens assemblies for robot (PAA5100JE) and drone (PMW3901) odometry; 28-pin packages; 4-wire SPI.
participants_or_bench: Manufacturer characterisation on crimson carpet, grey vinyl, replicated wood / light grey cement
key_quantitative_findings: PAA5100JE: working height 15-35 mm; frame rate 242 fps (4.13 ms/frame, derived); speed 45 ips at Z = 25 mm; repeated error 0.4% (up to 10 ips) and 2.8% (up to 45 ips) at Z = 25 mm; effective viewing angle 42 deg; needs external illumination (white LED LTW-216TS5, >= 15 mA); SPI <= 2 MHz; 6 mA chip-only run current; LGA + L214-ZSZ lens 6 x 6 x 3.08 mm; no lens focusing needed; 50 ms from reset to valid motion. PMW3901: working range 80 mm to infinity; speed 7.4 rad/s; 42 deg viewing angle; 9 mA run (v1.00); COB + LN03-ZSZ lens 6 x 6 x 2.28 mm; frame rate NOT stated in v1.00/v1.10 as read; Pimoroni breakout listing states 121 fps (8.26 ms, derived). Neither datasheet gives a cpi figure (flow scales with height).
units_and_conditions: Datasheet recommended operating conditions; not tested on paper; performance beyond conditions not guaranteed.
locator: PAA5100JE v1.00: p.1 Key Parameters; p.4 Table 3; p.5 Tables 4-5; p.6 Table 6. PMW3901 v1.00: p.1; p.3 Table 3. v1.10: p.1
limitations: No paper data; frame rates far below mouse sensors; count scale varies with height, so pen tilt changes calibration; PAA5100JE datasheet copy is a breakout-vendor mirror.
relevance_to_design: PAA5100JE is the one freely purchasable PixArt flow chip that works at pen-barrel distances (15-35 mm) - a candidate non-contact paper sensor mounted up the barrel; PMW3901 (>= 80 mm) is unsuitable near paper.
transferability_reason: Working range fits a barrel mount, but 242 fps and height-dependent scale limit loop bandwidth and accuracy; PMW3901 does not transfer.
design_implication: Test PAA5100JE on the bench as a barrel-mounted secondary sensor with IMU-based height/tilt scale correction; exclude PMW3901 from near-paper sensing.

topic: Capture pens: Anoto dot-pattern principle (patents and open codec)
citation: Anoto AB patents US6548768B1 'Determination of a position code' (priority 1999-10-01; published 2003-04-15) and US6663008B1 'Coding pattern and apparatus and method for determining a value of at least one mark of a coding pattern' (priority 1999-10-01; granted 2003-12-16); Heindl C., py-microdots (MIT-licensed Anoto codec) README.
task_or_setup: Absolute position coding: one mark per nominal raster point, displaced in one of four directions; the pen camera images a small window and decodes absolute x,y.
key_quantitative_findings: Raster spacing 300 um (range 250-300 um; 254 um variant for printers at multiples of 100 dpi); mark displacement 50 um (1/6 of the raster); embodiment sensor 'provides a new image every tenth millisecond' (~100 images/s) and sees about 10-12 marks per direction; example coding window of 4x4 symbols = 4^16 = 4,294,967,296 positions. py-microdots (describing the deployed pattern): every 6x6 dot window encodes a unique position at 0.3 mm grid (1.8 mm x 1.8 mm window, derived), unique over an area comparable to Europe and Asia. Positioning accuracy of commercial pens: NOT stated in these sources. Rough derivation: resolving 50 um offsets needs object-space sampling of roughly 25 um/pixel or finer.
units_and_conditions: Patent embodiments, not product specifications.
locator: US6548768B1 description (raster, displacement, image rate); US6663008B1 definitions and coding example; py-microdots README
limitations: Embodiments may differ from the commercial pattern; 6x6 details come from a third-party codec; no measured accuracy; the Google Patents record for US6548768B1 shows an expiry date of 2021-08-22, but freedom-to-operate for later Anoto patents was not assessed.
relevance_to_design: Printed-pattern paper gives the absolute page coordinates that note capture needs and relative flow cannot provide.
transferability_reason: Decoding physics transfers; using Anoto's pattern space is contractual; a self-made pattern needs its own IP review.
design_implication: Treat a printed position pattern as the proven route to absolute capture; if a tip camera is designed, target <= ~25 um/pixel object sampling and >= 75 Hz; commission a freedom-to-operate review before any own-pattern design.

topic: Capture pens: Anoto AP-701 pen and pattern licensing
citation: Anoto Support. 'Digital Pen comparison' (AP-701 vs AP-701C-M), last updated 28 Sep 2022; 'Pattern licenses', last updated 12 Nov 2020.
task_or_setup: Current Anoto camera pen hardware and the licensing model for the dot pattern.
key_quantitative_findings: AP-701: camera frame rate 75 FPS (13.3 ms, derived); camera activation 10 ms; 157.5 x 16.85 mm with cap; 18 g; Bluetooth 4.1 dual mode; AES256/RSA2048; D-1 ballpoint refill (1 mm); up to 10 h operation; 4 MB (~10 A4 pages) vs 128 MB (~410 A4 pages) on AP-701C-M. Pattern licences: unique pattern pages licensed singly, as 'books' or as 'shelves', on A3/A4 templates, exclusive 'for the duration of the subscription'. No positioning accuracy and no prices published on these pages.
units_and_conditions: Vendor documentation at retrieval date.
locator: Anoto Support articles 1626 and 414 (whole pages)
limitations: Vendor claims; no accuracy data; printing workflow (FDT tool, .oal licence file) seen only in a search snippet; commercial terms by negotiation.
relevance_to_design: Benchmarks a shipping capture-pen envelope (18 g, 16.85 mm) and shows pattern access is a recurring licence cost.
transferability_reason: Directly comparable capture pen and a licensable positioning system.
design_implication: If Anoto paper is used, budget a recurring pattern subscription; 75 FPS (13 ms) is far too slow for the stabilisation loop, so capture and stabilisation sensing must be separate channels.

topic: Inertial pens: why absolute position is unobservable (error-growth derivation)
citation: Analytical derivation in this ledger using STMicroelectronics LSM6DSL datasheet DocID028475 Rev 6 (May 2017) - the accelerometer/gyroscope in the STABILO DigiPen (see OPT-15).
task_or_setup: Dead-reckoning position error from double integration of accelerometer output, using datasheet offset and noise figures.
comparator: Optical-flow drift: DeltaPen idle translation drift 0.04375 mm/s (OPT-02)
key_quantitative_findings: Datasheet: zero-g offset +/-40 mg typ; zero-rate level +/-3 deg/s; acceleration noise density 90 ug/sqrt(Hz) (+/-2 g, high-performance); rate noise density 4 mdps/sqrt(Hz). Derived: constant accel bias b gives position error b*t^2/2 - 40 mg: 1.96 mm at 0.1 s, 196 mm at 1 s; 1 mg residual: 0.049 mm at 0.1 s, 4.9 mm at 1 s, 490 mm at 10 s. Gyro bias w tilts the gravity reference, error ~ g*w*t^3/6 - 3 deg/s: 0.086 mm at 0.1 s, 85.6 mm at 1 s. White noise alone: sigma_p ~ a_n*t^1.5/sqrt(3) = 0.51 mm at 1 s, 16 mm at 10 s. Accelerometers sense specific force (second derivative of position), so initial position and velocity are unobservable constants; yaw about the paper normal is unobservable from gravity; only short windows or zero-velocity updates (pen still) bound the error. Optical flow senses velocity, so its drift grows ~linearly (DeltaPen 2.6 mm/min idle) rather than quadratically.
units_and_conditions: Order-of-magnitude figures; perfect gravity removal assumed apart from the stated biases; g = 9.80665 m/s^2.
locator: LSM6DSL datasheet Table 3 'Mechanical characteristics' (pp.21-22); derivation in this row
limitations: Calibration, temperature compensation, ZUPT and fusion reduce but do not remove error growth; illustrative, not a measured pen.
relevance_to_design: Explains why inertial sensing can support tremor-band stabilisation (short horizon, high-pass) but cannot deliver page position for note capture.
transferability_reason: Physics independent of implementation.
design_implication: Use the IMU for tilt, tremor-band motion and gaps under ~0.1 s; require optical-flow or pattern sensing for anything longer; exploit pen-still periods for zero-velocity updates.

topic: Grounded generation evaluation: AIS (Attributable to Identified Sources)
citation: Rashkin H., Nikolaev V., Lamm M., Aroyo L., Collins M., Das D., Petrov S., Tomar G.S., Turc I., Reitter D. Measuring Attribution in Natural Language Generation Models. arXiv:2112.12870v2 (2 Aug 2022).
task_or_setup: Defines AIS: output is attributable if a generic reader would agree 'According to P, s'; two-stage human annotation (interpretability, then attribution) on conversational QA, CNN/DM summarisation and table-to-text.
participants_or_bench: Crowd annotators; 200 CNN/DM test examples per system
comparator: Extractive (MatchSum), hybrid (Pointer-Gen), abstractive (BigBird) and reference summaries
key_quantitative_findings: CNN/DM AIS: MatchSum 99.4%, Pointer-Gen 97.8%, BigBird 87.2%, gold reference summaries 54.1% (interpretability 86-90%). Inter-annotator agreement for AIS on CNN/DM: F1 0.92, pairwise agreement 0.89, Krippendorff's alpha 0.69 (interpretability alpha 0.46).
units_and_conditions: Summary-level judgements; percentages of outputs judged attributable.
locator: Sec. 3-4 (definition and pipeline); Table 5 (p.17); Table 7 (p.18)
limitations: News summaries, not personal notes; human-only protocol is costly; arXiv version read.
relevance_to_design: Supplies the definition and protocol for judging whether each summary statement is supported by the user's own notes.
transferability_reason: Source-agnostic definition; the 'source' becomes the note transcript.
design_implication: Adopt AIS-style two-stage human rating (interpretable? attributable to the cited note spans?) as the gold standard and report Krippendorff's alpha.
search_query: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.12870

topic: Grounded generation evaluation: FActScore (atomic-fact precision)
citation: Min S., Krishna K., Lyu X., Lewis M., Yih W., Koh P.W., Iyyer M., Zettlemoyer L., Hajishirzi H. FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation. arXiv:2305.14251v2 (11 Oct 2023).
task_or_setup: Split a generation into atomic facts; score = % of atomic facts supported by a knowledge source; human annotation plus an automated estimator (retrieval + LM).
participants_or_bench: Human annotators on people biographies; automated scoring of 6,500 generations from 13 LMs
key_quantitative_findings: Human FActScore: InstructGPT 42%, ChatGPT 58%, PerplexityAI 71%; automated estimator error rate < 2% vs human FActScore; scoring 6,500 generations with humans would have cost ~USD 26K.
units_and_conditions: Wikipedia as knowledge source; precision only.
locator: Abstract; Sec. 3 (human results); Table 3 (estimator error rates)
limitations: Biographies domain; estimator error higher for rare entities; no recall/coverage measure.
relevance_to_design: Atomic-fact support against the user's notes is a natural faithfulness metric for note summaries.
transferability_reason: Knowledge source becomes noisy recognised text; the estimator must be revalidated on notes.
design_implication: Score atomic facts against both the recognised text and the ground-truth transcript to separate recognition-induced from generation-induced errors.
search_query: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.14251

topic: Grounded generation evaluation: RAGAS (reference-free RAG metrics)
citation: Es S., James J., Espinosa-Anke L., Schockaert S. Ragas: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation. arXiv:2309.15217v2 (28 Apr 2025).
task_or_setup: LLM-based, reference-free metrics: faithfulness (answer statements supported by the retrieved context), answer relevance, context relevance; validated on the WikiEval set against human pairwise judgements.
participants_or_bench: Two human annotators (agreed in ~95% of cases for faithfulness and context relevance, ~90% for answer relevance)
comparator: GPT Score and GPT Ranking baselines
key_quantitative_findings: Agreement with human pairwise judgements (accuracy): faithfulness 0.95, answer relevance 0.78, context relevance 0.70 (GPT Score 0.72 / 0.52 / 0.63; GPT Ranking 0.54 / 0.40 / 0.52).
units_and_conditions: WikiEval; accuracy of pairwise preference.
locator: Sec. 3 (metrics); Sec. 4 (WikiEval); Table 1
limitations: Small evaluation set; depends on the judging LLM; measures faithfulness to retrieved context only.
relevance_to_design: Cheap automated faithfulness check for retrieval-grounded note Q&A and summaries.
transferability_reason: Needs recalibration on noisy handwritten-note text.
design_implication: Use RAGAS-style faithfulness as a regression metric in CI, recalibrated periodically against AIS human labels on our notes.
search_query: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.15217

topic: Grounded generation evaluation: ALCE citation recall/precision and audit of generative search
citation: Gao T., Yen H., Yu J., Chen D. Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations. arXiv:2305.14627v2 (31 Oct 2023) (ALCE); Liu N.F., Zhang T., Liang P. Evaluating Verifiability in Generative Search Engines. arXiv:2304.09848v2 (23 Oct 2023).
task_or_setup: Citation recall (each statement fully supported by its citations, judged by the NLI model TRUE, T5-11B) and citation precision (each citation needed/relevant); human audit of commercial generative search engines.
participants_or_bench: ALCE: human evaluation of model outputs; Liu et al.: human audit of four generative search engines
comparator: Human judgements vs automatic NLI metric
key_quantitative_findings: ALCE: on ELI5 even the best models lack complete citation support ~50% of the time; human-vs-automatic Cohen's kappa 0.698 (citation recall) and 0.525 (citation precision); automatic metric accuracy vs human labels 85.1% (recall) and 77.6% (precision). Liu et al.: 51.5% of generated sentences fully supported by citations; 74.5% of citations support their sentence.
units_and_conditions: Open-domain QA / web search.
locator: ALCE Abstract, Sec. 3 (metrics), Sec. 6 (human evaluation); Liu et al. Abstract
limitations: Not personal notes; NLI models may mishandle misrecognised words.
relevance_to_design: Defines per-statement citation metrics for 'source-grounded' summaries.
transferability_reason: Metric definitions transfer directly; the NLI judge needs validation on noisy notes.
design_implication: Require each summary sentence to cite note/page/stroke spans; report citation recall and precision (NLI plus human audit) and use these published figures as minimum baselines.
search_query: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.14627; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2304.09848
